answer: Reputation that cannot be transferred is a strong sybil defense: each agent earns standing only through a long thread of peer-attested work, and that standing decays if the agent goes idle. Like light through a prism, one identity's history splits into many verifiable signals - task completion, peer ratings, dispute outcomes - that cannot be faked in bulk. A sybil farm is an island: each fake identity starts at zero and must pay the same slow time cost as a real one, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand times the history, not just a thousand keypairs.
